name: Federal government
description: A U.S. government agency, the military, a federal site or a bank run by the FDIC.

name: Airline, Amtrak, long-distance bus
description: Airlines, Amtrak and long-distance buses. Federal law covers these instead.

name: Government benefits decision
description: A government decision about benefits, like unemployment, SNAP, Medicaid or Section 8 eligibility.

name: Court decision
description: What a court or judge decided, like in housing court, custody or child support.

name: A person, not a covered business
description: Another tenant, neighbor, roommate, customer or family member, rather than a landlord, employer or business.

name: Police
description: Police actions, like an arrest or a stop.

name: Prison or jail
description: How someone was treated in a prison, jail or other corrections facility.

name: Not discrimination
description: Unfair treatment not linked to a protected characteristic, like unpaid wages or a bad landlord.

name: Child protective services
description: How CPS or ACS handled a case.

name: Religious exemption
description: A religious group acting on its religion, like hiring clergy or running a religious school, event or housing.

name: Housing exceptions
description: Rentals the law exempts, like a room in the owner’s home, a two-family house the owner lives in, or senior housing.

name: Characteristic not covered in this area
description: A characteristic the law doesn’t protect in this area, like age at a store or family status at a school.

name: Retaliation not about discrimination
description: Punished for something other than opposing discrimination, like whistleblowing or reporting unsafe conditions.

name: Untimely
description: The last incident happened too long ago to file (past the statute of limitations).

name: Family member as employer
description: The employer is the person’s parent, spouse or child.
group: Complainant not covered or no standing

name: Conviction record outside employment
description: A conviction record held against someone outside work or licensing, like for housing.

name: Port Authority
description: The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, which both states run.

name: UN, embassy or consulate
description: The UN, or a foreign embassy or consulate, as employer. They have diplomatic immunity.

name: Political views
description: Political views or party, which the law doesn’t protect.

name: Homelessness
description: Being homeless, which the law doesn’t protect.

name: Credit history
description: Credit history, which state law doesn’t protect.

name: Open ACS or CPS case
description: Having an open child protective case, which the law doesn’t protect.

name: Height or weight
description: Height or weight, which state law doesn’t protect.

name: Current illegal drug use
description: Current illegal drug use. People in recovery are still protected under disability.

name: Lack of military service
description: Not having served in the military. Only military service is protected.

name: Family status: child’s needs
description: A child’s needs, like time off for school meetings or childcare. Family status covers being a parent, not the child’s needs.

name: Source of income: loans or whose income
description: Needing a loan, or whose income it is in the household. Source of income doesn’t cover these.

name: Arrest record: pending or not in favor
description: An arrest that’s still pending, or didn’t end in the person’s favor.

name: Conviction after hire
description: A conviction that happened after the person was hired. Only earlier convictions are protected.

name: Age under 18
description: Under 18. Age protection starts at 18.

name: Unpaid intern: arrest or conviction
description: An unpaid intern’s arrest or conviction record. Interns aren’t protected for these.

name: Tribal nation
description: A business run by a recognized Native American tribe, which has sovereign immunity.

name: Employee benefit plan (ERISA)
description: A work benefit plan under federal law (ERISA), for treatment federal law allows, like marital status.

name: NYS Justice Center
description: A decision by the NYS Justice Center for the Protection of People with Special Needs.

name: Government permit decision
description: A government decision about a permit.

name: Insurance
description: Selling insurance or what a policy covers, unless it’s part of something NYDHR covers, like job benefits.

name: Volunteer EMS
description: A volunteer ambulance or EMS squad. Only volunteer fire departments are covered.

name: Online ads
description: An ad posted online, which may not be covered the way print ads are.

name: Single-sex exemption
description: A single-sex school, or a place NYDHR has allowed to limit by sex.

name: Transit disability accommodation
description: Public transit, like the MTA or city buses, not giving a disability accommodation. Other discrimination by them is covered.

name: Age exceptions
description: Ages the law lets employers use, like 18–21 at bars, police and firefighter hiring ages, or some retirement ages.

name: Conviction record exceptions
description: Cases where a conviction can count, like law enforcement jobs, gun licenses, an offense linked to the job, or employers with under 10 staff.

name: Enforcing an earlier order or settlement
description: Getting someone to follow an earlier ruling or settlement on the same complaint.

name: No legal authority
description: Filed for someone else without legal authority, like guardianship or power of attorney.
group: Complainant not covered or no standing

name: Unclear who or what (call us)
description: Not enough detail about who did it to tell if NYDHR covers them.

name: Filer under 18
description: The person filing is under 18.
group: Complainant not covered or no standing

name: Filed elsewhere
description: The same events were already filed in court or with another agency.

name: Outside New York
description: It happened outside New York, or the business is based outside New York.

name: Unclear or unfocused report
description: The report is hard to follow, or lists many claims against several parties.

name: Section 8 voucher only
description: Refused only because of a Section 8 voucher. On hold while the courts decide, not dismissed.

name: Volunteer (not employee)
description: A volunteer, not an employee. May still be covered, so check with a supervisor.
group: Complainant not covered or no standing

name: No adverse action yet
description: Nothing has happened yet, or a single offhand remark with nothing after it.

name: Returned to EEOC
description: Sent back to the U.S. EEOC to handle.

name: Fake or no connection
description: The report seems fake, or the filer has no connection to the person it happened to.

name: Withdrawn or abandoned
description: The person withdrew, didn’t sign, or never followed up.

name: Remote employee
description: A remote worker whose worksite may not be in New York. Check with a supervisor.

name: Labor boycott
description: A boycott connected with a labor dispute, like a strike or picket line. The law exempts these.

name: Boycott to protest discrimination
description: A boycott held to protest unlawful discrimination. The law exempts these.

name: Distinctly private club or place
description: A club or place that is truly private and not open to the public, so it isn’t a place of public accommodation.

name: Conviction record: public employer or agency
description: A government employer or licensing agency held a conviction against someone. These go to state court (Article 78), not NYDHR.
